content: 1. Ciprofloxacin increases the levels of pomalidomide by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 2. Ponatinib increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids, such as ciprofloxacin and prednisolone, may increase the risk of tendon rupture. Monitor patients closely for this adverse effect. 4. Pretomanid significantly inhibits OAT3 in vitro, which may increase ciprofloxacin levels and adverse effects. Consider dosage reduction of OAT3 substrates and monitor closely. 5. Ciprofloxacin and primaquine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 6. Probenecid interferes with the renal tubular secretion of ciprofloxacin, leading to increased serum levels of ciprofloxacin. Monitor for potential toxicity. 7. Ciprofloxacin and procainamide both increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 8. Ciprofloxacin minimally affects the QT interval but should be used cautiously in combination with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors for QT prolongation. 9. Ciprofloxacin increases propranolol levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 10. Ciprofloxacin decreases pyridoxine levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 11. Ciprofloxacin increases quazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Quercetin decreases the effects of ciprofloxacin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 13. Ciprofloxacin and quetiapine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid use with other QT-prolonging drugs and monitor patients closely with ECG. 14. Quinapril decreases ciprofloxacin levels due to chelation. Separate doses by at least 2 hours to minimize interaction. 15. Ciprofloxacin and quinidine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 16. Ciprofloxacin and quinine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 17. Quizartinib and ciprofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor patients closely with ECG and consider therapy modification. 18. Ciprofloxacin increases ramelteon levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity if co-administered. 19. Ciprofloxacin and ranolazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 20. Ciprofloxacin increases rasagiline levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism, potentially leading to increased adverse reactions. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 21. Ciprofloxacin increases repaglinide effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor blood glucose levels closely for hyperor hypoglycemia. 22. Ribociclib increases ciprofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 23. Rilpivirine increases ciprofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 24. Ciprofloxacin increases riluzole levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity if co-administered. 25. Ciprofloxacin increases ropinirole levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor for increased effects of ropinirole. 26. Ciprofloxacin increases ropivacaine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor for signs of ropivacaine toxicity. 27. Ciprofloxacin increases rosiglitazone effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor blood glucose levels closely for hyperor hypoglycemia. 28. Ciprofloxacin increases ruxolitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 29. Sarecycline increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities and consider dosage adjustments. 30. Ciprofloxacin increases saxagliptin effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Monitor blood glucose levels closely for hyperor hypoglycemia. 31. Sodium bicarbonate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by reducing gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor for crystalluria and nephrotoxicity due to alkaline urine. 32. Sodium citrate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by reducing gastrointestinal absorption. Monitor for crystalluria and nephrotoxicity due to alkaline urine. 33. Sodium picosulfate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after sodium picosulfate. 34. Magnesium sulfate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by reducing gastrointestinal absorption. Administer ciprofloxacin at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium sulfate. 35. Ciprofloxacin and solifenacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 36. Ciprofloxacin and sorafenib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 37. Ciprofloxacin and sotalol both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 38. Sotorasib decreases ciprofloxacin levels by inducing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or adjust dosages as needed. 39. Stiripentol increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider reducing the dose of P-gp substrates if adverse reactions occur. 40. Sucralfate decreases ciprofloxacin levels by chelation in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after sucralfate. 41. Ciprofloxacin and sulindac may increase the risk of CNS stimulation and seizures at high doses. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 42. Ciprofloxacin and sunitinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 43. Ciprofloxacin and tacrolimus both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 44. Ciprofloxacin increases tasimelteon levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid co-administration due to the risk of adverse reactions. 45. Ciprofloxacin and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 46. Ciprofloxacin increases temazepam levels by decreasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 47. Tepotinib increases ciprofloxacin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or adjust dosages as needed. 48. Ciprofloxacin increases terbinafine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity if co-administered. 49. Ciprofloxacin and tetrabenazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation. 50. Ciprofloxacin increases theophylline levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism, leading to decreased clearance and increased toxicity. Avoid co-administration or monitor theophylline levels closely. 51. Ciprofloxacin decreases thiamine levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. 52. Ciprofloxacin and thioridazine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor for QT prolongation.
